obligations.note: At head, privileged sessions idle between 15 and 16 minutes are accepted (PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES=16 > 15), so this breaches the obligation as written. The control test passes only because it checks against the edited policy-params.json. The breach is covered by exception EXC-0224 (see EXC-1).

EXC-0224 is approved by Helena Vasquez (risk_owner, CISO office), not by the requester Linh Nguyen. It expires 2026-11-25, after the 2026-10-26 review time. It is scoped to SES-1 / payments.session for 'all Payments privileged sessions using the sixteen-minute idle interval' and records a compensating control.
Ticket CHG-26135 was approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-20, before the PR opened on 2026-10-23. Its components (payments.policy, payments.controls-data) cover both changed paths.
The code_review approval is from Mara Costa, a change_approver for payments and a different person from the author Linh Nguyen.
The code_review and control_owner approvals both name the head commit dcf5be9, which is the change's only commit.

CI run pr-checks on head dcf5be9 succeeded: 172 tests across all 28 payments test files, 0 failures, 0 skipped. That includes the SES-1 control test test_privileged_idle_timeout_within_policy, the only product obligation whose scope the change touches. I couldn't rerun the suite (pytest isn't installed). The report names a different host than the CI runner (dev-laptop-7.local vs ci-runner-09).
The touched components payments.policy and payments.controls-data are not security_sensitive, so no security_review is required.
The protected path controls/payments/policy-params.json changed (an approved policy value). Rachel Stein (control_owner, controls-office, not the author's payments-eng team) approved the head commit.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not an emergency, so no PIR is due.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers the changed code. The only behavioural change is PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES, and no ledger entry covers that symbol or session.py, so no accepted evidence lapses.

summary: The change raises Payments' privileged idle timeout from 15 to 16 minutes, which breaches SES-1 as written. A valid exception, EXC-0224, covers it: approved by a CISO-office risk owner who is not the requester, unexpired at review time, scoped to SES-1 and payments.session, and recording a compensating control. The process records are complete: the ticket was approved in advance and covers the touched components, the independent code review and outside-team control-owner approval both name the head commit, and the CI run on head is green and includes the SES-1 control test. No security review is needed and no ledger evidence lapses, so the change can be accepted.
